trail.text: Memory pressure and latency spikes — tracing the failure outward.
Orders and front-end show the sharpest latency climbs — now checking neighboring services for the origin.
Timing points to the edge first, but severity points inward — digging into the sequence to separate cause from victim.
Tail latency in orders looks earliest — verifying the propagation timeline.
Orders and user broke together — checking the backing stores for the underlying fault.

causes.reasoning: Orders shows the strongest median latency jump 0.016 to 0.11 with tail 0.023 to 0.42 starting at ~13s, plus CPU rise, indicating the primary queuing point that propagates to front-end.
User tail latency jumps 0.009 to 0.24 at the same early time with flat-to-down CPU/memory, classic victim waiting on downstream but co-incident with orders suggesting coupled failure.
Front-end tail latency 0.069 to 0.31 ramps slightly after orders/user with median almost flat, consistent with downstream orders/user slowness making the edge look unhealthy.
User-db memory and cache steadily grow 69M to 75M with increased fs IO, plausible slowdown of user queries that would explain user service tail latency.
Orders-db memory/cache grows 48M to 51M through the window, a possible downstream pressure contributing to orders CPU and latency rise.
